name: Repetition of the divine name on beads (nāma-japa)
method_summary: Softly repeating the names of Kṛṣṇa (in Gauḍīya practice, above all the Hare Kṛṣṇa mahāmantra) on a string of tulasī beads, attentively and free of the ten offences; Haridāsa Ṭhākura's daily vow of three hundred thousand names is the model; later institutions fix a daily minimum (e.g. ISKCON's sixteen rounds, recent). In the Puṣṭimārga the refuge mantra 'śrī kṛṣṇaḥ śaraṇaṃ mama' is repeated.
signs_of_progress: tears, faltering voice, horripilation while chanting (Śikṣāṣṭaka 6)

warnings.text: Chanting while committing the ten offences does not yield love; sinning on the strength of the name is itself an offence.

equivalents.note: general mantra repetition; here the object is the name itself, held non-different from Kṛṣṇa

name: Congregational chanting of the name (nāma-saṅkīrtana)
method_summary: Singing the Lord's names together, aloud, with drums (khol/mṛdaṅga) and cymbals, in homes, temples and street processions (nagara-saṅkīrtana), led by a lead singer with response; held to be the dharma of Kali and the most potent limb; to be done with humility (Śikṣāṣṭaka 3).

equivalents.note: the Purāṇic kīrtana; Gauḍīya saṅkīrtana is congregational and name-centred

name: The Hare Kṛṣṇa mahāmantra
method_summary: The sixteen names 'hare kṛṣṇa hare kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa hare hare / hare rāma hare rāma rāma rāma hare hare' (the Kalisantaraṇa gives the Hare Rāma half first), chanted in japa or sung in kīrtana; the Upaniṣad states there are no rules of time, place or purity for it.

name: The sixty-four limbs of devotional practice
method_summary: Rūpa's list of practices: the first ten (taking shelter of a guru, initiation and instruction, serving the guru with trust, following the saints, inquiring into true dharma, renouncing enjoyment for Kṛṣṇa, residence at holy places, accepting only what is needed, honouring Ekādaśī, honouring the sacred trees, cows and brāhmaṇas) and ten avoidances (of non-devotees' company, many disciples, great undertakings, many books for argument, miserliness, grief, disrespect of other gods, harming beings, offences in worship and to the name, tolerating blasphemy) are the gateway; then hearing, chanting, remembering, worship, bowing, prayer, service, friendship, self-offering, wearing Vaiṣṇava marks, honouring prasāda, tulasī, festivals and more, ending with the five most potent limbs.
notes: The full list of sixty-four is recalled only in part; verse-by-verse list to be extracted in Phase D.

name: The five most potent limbs of devotion
method_summary: Serving the deity with faith, relishing the Bhāgavata with the like-minded, association with advanced devotees, congregational chanting of the name, and residence in Mathurā/Vraja; even slight contact with them awakens love.

name: Rule-based devotional practice (vaidhī sādhana)
method_summary: Performing the limbs of devotion — hearing, chanting, worship, fasts, vows — because scripture commands them, under a guru, until spontaneous attraction arises.

name: Spontaneous devotional practice (rāgānugā sādhana)
method_summary: Driven by eager longing for a Vraja resident's love, the practitioner continues external practice in the body while inwardly remembering Kṛṣṇa and the chosen associate and serving in the inner perfected body, living (physically or mentally) in Vraja and following those who love him.
prerequisites: guidance of a guru in the chosen mood

warnings.text: Semblances of emotion (ratyābhāsa) in those whose hearts are impure are not bhāva; outward signs alone do not prove love.

name: Remembrance of the eightfold daily play (aṣṭakālīya-līlā-smaraṇa)
method_summary: Meditative remembrance of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa's pastimes through the eight periods of the day, following texts such as the Govindalīlāmṛta and Kṛṣṇabhāvanāmṛta, often in one's inner identity as a mañjarī serving Rādhā; given within a guru's transmission.
prerequisites: guru's instruction in the inner identity (siddha-praṇālī) in lineages that give it

warnings.text: The Gosvāmīs require eagerness born of grace and purification from offences; later teachers (Bhaktisiddhānta, recent) warned against premature imitation of this practice.

name: Gauḍīya initiation (dīkṣā)
method_summary: After mutual examination, the guru gives the disciple the Kṛṣṇa mantras (the eighteen-syllable gopāla-mantra and the kāma-gāyatrī, among others), tilaka and neck-beads; initiation makes one fit for deity worship. The mantras are given privately and are not recorded here.

name: Surrender (prapatti / śaraṇāgati)
method_summary: Taking refuge in the Lord alone: resolving to do what pleases him, rejecting what displeases him, trusting his protection, choosing him as protector, offering oneself and living in humility.

name: Surrender to the guru (gurūpasatti)
method_summary: The fifth means of the Nimbārka school: complete dependence on the guru, who then performs the means on the disciple's behalf.

name: Worship of the divine couple (yugala-upāsanā)
method_summary: Worship and meditation on Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa together — Rādhā on Kṛṣṇa's left, served by the sakhīs — in the Nimbārka school, with Braj songs of the couple's play (Yugalaśataka, Mahāvāṇī).

name: Service of the Lord's form (puṣṭi sevā)
method_summary: Loving, householder service of Kṛṣṇa's image (svarūpa) as a living child and lord — waking, feeding, dressing, playing, resting him — with body, wealth and above all the mind; the fruit of service is more service.

name: The eightfold daily service (aṣṭayāma sevā)
method_summary: Viṭṭhalanātha's ordering of the day into eight darśanas: maṅgalā, śṛṅgāra, gvāla, rājabhoga, utthāpana, bhoga, sandhyā-ārtī, śayana, each with its offerings, dress and songs of the aṣṭachāp.

name: Brahmasambandha initiation
method_summary: The second initiation of the Puṣṭimārga, following the refuge mantra: the disciple, holding tulasī, dedicates body, senses, life, mind and possessions to Kṛṣṇa through a formula given privately by a Gosvāmī ācārya; thereafter everything is offered before use.

name: Offering before use (samarpaṇa)
method_summary: Nothing unoffered is used: food, clothes and all things are first offered to the Lord and then accepted as his grace.

name: Havelī kīrtan
method_summary: Temple singing of the aṣṭachāp poets' songs in classical rāgas matched to each period of the day and season, as part of the Lord's service.

name: Combining knowledge with works
method_summary: Continuing the Vedic and social duties of one's station throughout life together with meditation on Brahman, rather than renouncing works after knowledge.

name: Meditation on the small space in the heart (dahara-vidyā)
method_summary: Meditation on Brahman within the small space of the heart-lotus (Chāndogya 8.1); for Śrīkaṇṭha, meditation on Śiva as the supreme ether, his cit-śakti.

name: Ekādaśī fast
method_summary: Fasting from grains (or fully) on the eleventh lunar day, with extra hearing and chanting; obligatory for Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇavas (Haribhaktivilāsa).

name: Service of tulasī
method_summary: Watering, circumambulating and worshipping the tulasī plant, beloved of Kṛṣṇa, and wearing and chanting on tulasī beads.

name: Circumambulation of Vraja (vraja-parikramā)
method_summary: Pilgrimage around the sites of Kṛṣṇa's play in Braj (Govardhana, Rādhākuṇḍa, the forests), done by Gauḍīyas and the Puṣṭimārga (whose ban-yātrā follows Vallabha's seats); residence in Vraja is one of the five potent limbs.

name: Purification of the elements (bhūta-śuddhi)
method_summary: In Gauḍīya deity worship (Haribhaktivilāsa, following Pāñcarātra and tantric manuals), the worshipper purifies the elements of the body by meditation and places mantras on the limbs (nyāsa) before worship.

name: Ritual worship (pūjā)
method_summary: Gauḍīya deity worship (arcana, śrī-mūrti-sevā) according to the Haribhaktivilāsa, with offerings, ārati and prasāda; serving the deity with faith is one of the five most potent limbs. Puṣṭimārga service of the Lord's form (sevā) in the havelī follows the eight daily periods.

name: Devotional singing (kīrtana)
method_summary: Gauḍīya congregational singing of the name and of Rādhā–Kṛṣṇa's play (with khol and karatāla; later padāvalī-kīrtana styles); Puṣṭimārga havelī kīrtan of the aṣṭachāp songs.
